headline: Forged in operations.
Engineered for the cloud.
hero.subheadline: AWS Certified Solutions Architect. Built to withstand production traffic. Available 2026.
hero.footnote: Every resource behind this page was provisioned by Terraform and deployed by a pipeline that holds no AWS keys.

highlights.label: certifications earned
highlights.detail: AWS Solutions Architect Associate, AWS Cloud Practitioner, Linux Essentials, Oracle Cloud Foundations, Google IT Support.

highlights.label: events ingested from a live honeypot
highlights.detail: A deliberately exposed host inside a locked down VPC streamed unsolicited internet traffic into Splunk. The attacker addresses in those dashboards are organic, not simulated.

highlights.label: of this stack is code
highlights.detail: No console clicks. Every bucket, role, function, table and DNS record lives in a Terraform module.

highlights.label: long lived keys in CI
highlights.detail: GitHub authenticates to AWS over OpenID Connect. The credentials expire in one hour and are never stored.

projects.title: Enterprise DevSecOps Threat Pipeline
projects.summary: Splunk ingests VPC Flow Logs and CloudTrail, correlation searches mapped to MITRE ATT&CK raise the alert, and a Python Lambda drops a deny rule into the network ACL before a human has read the notification.
projects.detail: I own every piece of AWS infrastructure and all of the Terraform. Kenny Barr owns the Splunk detection engineering and the dashboard work.

media.alt: Splunk dashboard titled Phase 1 Cryptojacking Detection. An endpoint malware event mapped to MITRE technique T1496 with high severity, an attack timeline broken out by source address, port sweep activity, a threat correlation summary, and a table of the top attacking addresses with their connection counts and targeted ports.

projects.title: SecureAccess Audit Dashboard
projects.summary: Parses raw access logs in the browser and scores every session against several risk signals at once, so a reviewer opens the three accounts worth investigating instead of scrolling ten thousand rows.

media.alt: The SecureAccess Audit Dashboard. Four summary tiles reading 44 total events, 17 failed logins, 5 flagged accounts and a highest risk user, a row of filter tabs for failed logins, after hours activity, privilege escalation and suspicious only, and a table of access events with usernames, actions, addresses, departments, status and a threat score per row.

projects.title: AWS Incident Response Honeypot
projects.summary: A deliberately exposed host inside a locked down VPC, provisioned by Terraform, that streamed unsolicited attack traffic into Splunk. The threat actor data in these dashboards is organic, not simulated.

media.alt: Splunk panel showing an automation KPI of 77,959 events, beside a statistics table of attacking source addresses with connection counts and the most recent port each one targeted.

projects.title: Serverless Resume Platform
projects.summary: React on a private S3 bucket behind CloudFront, a Python Lambda counting visits in DynamoDB, and a pipeline that plans before a human approves the apply.

projects.title: RHEL LogVault Automation
projects.summary: Scheduled shell and systemd automation that collects, compresses and ships RHEL 9 journal data with integrity checks, so a rotated log cannot be quietly altered.

items: AWS: EC2, VPC, S3, IAM, Lambda, DynamoDB, CloudFront, Route53, API Gateway, CloudWatch, WAF
Cost aware architecture and on demand capacity choices
Terraform, written as reusable modules with typed variables and validation
Remote state in S3 with DynamoDB locking
Plan review discipline. Nothing reaches production without a readable diff
Splunk SPL, CIM normalization, correlation searches
CloudTrail and VPC Flow Log analysis
Automated containment with Lambda and network ACLs
GitHub Actions with OpenID Connect federation
pytest and moto for AWS unit tests
Least privilege deploy roles, separated for plan and apply
Cache invalidation and immutable asset strategy
